identity.title: An NLR Associated With Defence Against Turnip Mosaic Virus in Nicotiana benthamiana.

content.abstract: While the role of nucleotide-binding leucine-rich repeat (NLR) proteins as intracellular immune receptors in plants is well documented, information on NLRs involved in antiviral defence remains scarce. Here, we conducted a high-throughput virus-induced gene silencing (VIGS) screen of 301 NLRs in Nicotiana benthamiana using turnip mosaic virus (TuMV) to identify NLRs potentially involved in TuMV infection. Genetic analyses identified that NLR39-2, a previously uncharacterized Toll/interleukin-1 receptor NLR, enhanced antiviral defence: overexpression suppressed TuMV accumulation, whereas CRISPR-Cas9 knockout enhanced susceptibility. This enhanced defence is probably specific to TuMV, as NLR39-2 manipulation did not affect infection by the related potyvirus chilli veinal mottle virus or the unrelated potato virus X. Mechanistically, NLR39-2 was transcriptionally upregulated upon infection and physically interacted with the viral protein VPg. Co-expression with individual TuMV proteins did not trigger hypersensitive cell death. During infection, NLR39-2 partially redistributed from the plasma membrane to cytoplasmic P-bodies, which are tightly associated with the viral replication complexes. Our study establishes a scalable platform for antiviral NLR discovery and provides a new NLR resource for engineering TuMV resistance.
